Validate text in a Unicode encoding

Source: R/validate.R
utf_valid.Rd

utf_valid() tells whether each element is well-formed in encoding. utf_error_at() gives the position of its first error. utf_is_ascii() tells whether each element is pure ASCII, bytes 0x00 to 0x7F.

Usage

utf_valid(x, encoding = "UTF-8", useBytes = FALSE)

utf_error_at(x, encoding = "UTF-8", useBytes = FALSE)

utf_is_ascii(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector, a raw vector (one element), or a list of raw vectors (one element each). NA strings and NULL list elements give NA.

encoding

The encoding to check against: "UTF-8", "UTF-16LE", "UTF-16BE", "UTF-16", "UTF-32LE", "UTF-32BE", "UTF-32", "Latin-1" or "ASCII", matched without regard to case or hyphens ("utf8" is "UTF-8"). A character vector is UTF-8 text, so for one only "UTF-8" and "ASCII" apply unless useBytes = TRUE.

useBytes

For a character vector: FALSE (the default) takes each string in its marked encoding and checks its UTF-8 form, refusing strings marked "bytes"; TRUE checks the bytes of every string as they are, which is how to check a string R believes is UTF-8.

Value

utf_valid() and utf_is_ascii(): a logical vector, one value per element. utf_error_at(): an integer vector of 1-based offsets of the first error, in the input's code units (bytes for UTF-8, Latin-1 and ASCII; 16-bit units for UTF-16; 32-bit units for UTF-32), counted after any byte-order mark, and NA where the element is valid. A character vector or a list keeps its names.

Details

Well-formed means what Unicode says: in UTF-8, no overlong forms, no encoded surrogates (U+D800 to U+DFFF), nothing above U+10FFFF and no truncated sequence; in UTF-16, no unpaired surrogate; in UTF-32, no surrogate and nothing above U+10FFFF. A UTF-16 or UTF-32 input whose length is not a whole number of code units is ill-formed at its last, partial unit. Every byte string is valid Latin-1.

A leading byte-order mark that matches encoding is skipped. With "UTF-16" or "UTF-32", a byte-order mark chooses the byte order, and without one the input is big-endian.

See also

utf_count(); validUTF8(), which answers yes or no for UTF-8 only.

Examples

utf_valid(c("abc", "caf\u00e9", NA))
#> [1] TRUE TRUE   NA
utf_valid(as.raw(c(0xc3, 0x28)))            # a truncated sequence
#> [1] FALSE
utf_error_at(as.raw(c(0x61, 0x62, 0xff)))   # third byte
#> [1] 3

# UTF-16 with and without a byte-order mark
le <- as.raw(c(0xff, 0xfe, 0x61, 0x00, 0x00, 0xd8))
utf_valid(le, "UTF-16")                     # the BOM says little-endian
#> [1] FALSE
utf_error_at(le, "UTF-16LE")                # unpaired surrogate, unit 2
#> [1] 2

# several byte strings at once
utf_valid(list(charToRaw("ok"), as.raw(0xc0), NULL))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA

utf_is_ascii(c("abc", "caf\u00e9"))
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE
